idiom_name: nested def with nonlocal; callable class when the algorithm must be an object
implementation_notes: A nested def closes over the enclosing call's locals and nonlocal lets it rebind them (Python reference: simple statements), so a long method becomes a small family of inner functions sharing one frame - the closure cell is the method object's field set; functools.partial is enough when a step only needs arguments frozen. Keep the classic class with __call__ (or a dataclass with methods) when the algorithm must be picklable, inspected, subclassed or unit-tested as a named unit, or when it exposes more than one operation.
pitfalls: Without a nonlocal declaration an assignment inside the inner function creates a new local, and the next read raises UnboundLocalError.
Closures bind variables, not values: functions created in a loop all see the final loop variable unless it is bound per iteration through a default argument or a factory function.
Closures cannot be pickled, so a computation that must cross a process boundary has to be a class.
